title: Are LLMs Empathetic to All? Investigating the Influence of Multi-Demographic Personas on a Model’s Empathy
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the variation in empathetic responses (both affective and cognitive) of Large Language Models towards user personas from different cultural groups, several of which are defined by religious affiliation (e.g., Protestant Europe, Catholic Europe, African-Islamic, Orthodox Europe, Confucian).
findings: LLMs exhibit notable variations in empathy across different faith-affiliated cultural groups. Personas from Confucian culture consistently received responses with lower emotional intensity and cognitive empathy across all tested models. Models tended to overemphasize cultural contexts for groups like Confucian, African-Islamic, and Latin American cultures, leading to stereotypical understanding at the expense of emotional depth. Furthermore, log-odds analysis of generated responses showed models associated words like 'prayer', 'piety', and 'forgiveness' with specific religious cultures, such as Protestant, Catholic, and Orthodox Europe.
